title: Attorney General of Minnesota

context.text: Ellison won the August 11, 2026 DFL primary over David Madgett, 573,186 votes (85%) to 103,743 (15%) in WDIO's results display; Ronald J. Schutz was unopposed for the Republican nomination.

KAXE's election guide and The Green Papers (which compiles state candidate filings) both list only Ellison and Schutz as candidates for attorney general; the Minnesota Secretary of State's official candidate-filing site could not be queried without a form submission and was not checked directly.

candidates.name: Keith Ellison
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 11, 2026 DFL primary.

summary.text: Keith Ellison is the incumbent DFL Attorney General of Minnesota, seeking a third term. Before becoming attorney general in 2019 he served in the Minnesota House and then in the U.S. House for Minnesota's 5th District; as attorney general his office has prosecuted Medicaid and child-nutrition fraud and brought consumer, antitrust and multistate suits against corporations and the Trump administration.

background.text: Served in the Minnesota House of Representatives (District 58B) from 2003 through 2006 and as U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 5th District from January 2007 to January 2019.
Took office as Minnesota Attorney General in January 2019 and describes himself as having been elected to two terms; lists his community as North Minneapolis.

priorities.text: Helping Minnesotans afford their lives by taking on unlawful practices that raise prices, such as insulin pricing, John Deere repair restrictions and meatpacker price-fixing.
Prosecuting fraud and violent crime; he cites more than 350 Medicaid fraud convictions and the Medicaid Assistance Protection Act, which he says raises penalties and adds investigators.
Protecting Minnesota from federal actions he calls overreach; he says he has protected over $7.3 billion in funding from federal cuts.

record.text: Filed a Minnesota False Claims Act civil lawsuit and an $18.5 million consent judgment with nonprofit Partners in Nutrition over claims for child nutrition meals that were not delivered; the group agreed to dissolve.

Reached a settlement with John Deere resolving his January 2025 antitrust suit (with other states and the FTC), requiring Deere to make repair resources available to farmers and independent repairers for 10 years.
Won denial of TikTok's motion to dismiss Minnesota's lawsuit over app design aimed at young users and its TikTok LIVE virtual currency.
With 22 other attorneys general, won summary judgment in a federal court in Oregon holding that the CFPB must be lawfully funded, resolving a December 2025 suit.

candidates.name: Ronald J. Schutz

summary.text: Ron Schutz is the Republican nominee for Minnesota Attorney General. A Medina attorney, he is the former chairman of a national litigation firm and a former Army JAG Corps prosecutor, and is campaigning on prosecuting fraud, supporting law enforcement and keeping biological males from competing in girls' sports.

background.text: Former chairman of a 200-lawyer national litigation firm; began his career as a prosecutor in the U.S. Army JAG Corps.
Practices law through Schutz PLLC; lives in Medina.

priorities.text: Prosecuting fraudsters, supporting law enforcement, and restoring fairness in girls' sports.
Restoring integrity to the Attorney General's office and putting the interests of Minnesotans above politics.

positions.summary: Lists keeping biological males out of girls' sports as one of his top three priorities.
positions.quote: Restore fairness in girls sports by keeping biological males from competing against girls.

candidates.researchNotes: No elected office or official record was found or listed in his questionnaire. The campaign site ronformnag.com was named in the questionnaire but not separately loaded.
